body:
Two quantities are proportional when their ratio is always the same. That ratio is the constant of proportionality, k.

Three ways to spot a proportional relationship:
- The equation looks like y = kx.
- The table has the same y ÷ x in every row.
- The graph is a straight line through the origin, (0, 0).

Worked example: A printer prints 45 pages in 3 minutes at a steady rate.
k = 45 ÷ 3 = 15 pages per minute, so the equation is p = 15m.
In 8 minutes it prints 15 × 8 = 120 pages.
The point (1, 15) on the graph shows the unit rate: 15 pages in 1 minute.

Percents are proportional relationships too. 20% of a number is 0.20 times the number, so a 20% tip on a $30 bill is 0.20 × 30 = $6.

By the end of this unit you will be able to decide whether a relationship is proportional, find k from a table, graph, equation or story, and use proportions to solve percent problems about tax, tips, discounts and change.
title: Is It Proportional?
